findings.title: Org slug condition inverted: `!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED && { slug }` became `IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {}`
findings.body: The original code set `slug` only when team billing is disabled (when enabled, the slug is parked in `metadata.requestedSlug` until payment/verification). The rewrite drops the `!`, so with billing enabled the organization is created with the slug immediately (bypassing the requested-slug flow), and with billing disabled it is created with no slug at all. The `requestedSlug` line below (153) keeps the original polarity, so the two lines now contradict each other. This file is also unrelated to the destinationCalendar change. Restore `...(!IS_TEAM_BILLING_ENABLED ? { slug } : {})` or revert the hunk.

findings.title: TypeError when location is Google Meet and there is no destination calendar
findings.body: `const [mainHostDestinationCalendar] = evt.destinationCalendar ?? [];` yields `undefined` when `destinationCalendar` is null or empty, and line 119 then reads `mainHostDestinationCalendar.integration` without `?.`. handleNewBooking sets `destinationCalendar` to `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has one (handleNewBooking.ts:1063-1067), and the payment/confirm/reminder callers now pass `[]`. A booking with `location === MeetLocationType` and no destination calendar used to fall back to Cal Video (`evt.destinationCalendar?.integration`); now `create()` throws. Use `mainHostDestinationCalendar?.integration`.

findings.title: Video references no longer store credentialId, so cancelling skips deleting the meeting
findings.body: The old code stored `result.credentialId` for non-calendar results; the new code stores `isCalendarType ? result.credentialId : undefined`, so video references always get `credentialId` undefined, although `createMeeting` returns `credentialId: credential.id` (packages/core/videoClient.ts:78). handleCancelBooking only deletes the video meeting when `bookingVideoReference.credentialId` is set (handleCancelBooking.ts:491), so for every booking created after this change the Cal Video/Zoom/etc. meeting is silently left behind on cancel. Keep `credentialId: result.credentialId` for both types.

findings.title: Hangout-link patch uses `selectedCalendar` that can now be undefined
findings.body: `selectedCalendar` used to default to "primary"; now the default is applied only at insert (line 154: `selectedCalendar || "primary"`). The `events.patch` at line 166-177 still passes `calendarId: selectedCalendar`, which is undefined whenever no destination calendar matches the credential. The patch (which writes the Meet link into the description) is then sent without a calendarId and fails silently (no callback). Use the same `selectedCalendar || "primary"` value for the patch.

findings.title: Fallback to destination calendar in updateEvent/deleteEvent can never match
findings.body: The fallback branch only runs when `externalCalendarId` is falsy, and then searches `destinationCalendar` for `cal.externalId === externalCalendarId`, i.e. for an entry whose externalId equals a falsy value. It effectively always returns undefined. Before, it fell back to `event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`. For references without `externalCalendarId` (older bookings, or references created through the no-credentialId branch of createAllCalendarEvents), update now passes `calendarId: undefined` to Google (line 261), and delete drops to "primary" (line 317-322) even if the booking was on another calendar. Fall back to the first destination calendar's `externalId` (as the other services in this PR do) instead of searching by the falsy id. Same bug at line 317.

findings.title: createEvent ignores destination calendars that have no credentialId and goes to "primary"
findings.body: The target calendar is chosen only by `cal.credentialId === credentialId`. For a destination calendar with `credentialId` null, createAllCalendarEvents takes the else branch and calls `createEvent(c, event)` for every credential of that integration type (EventManager.ts:376-381). No entry then matches, so the event is inserted in "primary" instead of the selected `externalId` (previously `destinationCalendar.externalId`). The reference also gets `externalCalendarId` undefined (EventManager.ts:169 uses `result.externalId`, which is only set when `externalId` was passed to `createEvent`). Fall back to the destination calendar whose integration matches, and pass its externalId through in the else branch.

findings.title: updateLocation now writes calendar references without credentialId/externalCalendarId
findings.body: The references used to take `externalCalendarId` from `evt.destinationCalendar` and `credentialId` from `result.credentialId ?? destinationCalendar.credentialId`. Now both come from the result only, but `updateEvent` in CalendarManager returns neither `credentialId` nor `externalId` (packages/core/CalendarManager.ts:313-322). editLocation.handler.ts:120 creates these references on the booking, so calendar references created by an edit-location have both fields null. Later cancel/reschedule then falls into the no-credentialId path. Return `credentialId`/`externalId` from `updateEvent`, or carry them over from the existing references.

findings.title: Update failures are now swallowed silently and an unresolved credential is passed to updateEvent
findings.body: The catch block builds `message` but the `console.error(message)` that used to print it was removed, so `message` is unused and any exception in updateAllCalendarEvents (including a missing credential) now yields only a `success: false` result with no log. Also, when `reference.credentialId` is set but neither `this.calendarCredentials` nor the DB lookup (which also requires `app.slug`) yields a credential, `credential` stays undefined and is still passed to `updateEvent` (line 542), where `credential.appName` is read (CalendarManager.ts:314). That throws into this catch. Skip that reference explicitly, and keep the log line.

findings.title: Recurring-series deletion now repeats once per calendar reference
findings.body: The recurring branch (lines 444-468) deletes the calendar events of all `updatedBookings` using every user calendar credential, and does not depend on the current `reference`. Wrapping it in `for (const reference of bookingCalendarReference)` with a credentialId runs the whole series deletion once per reference. With the new multi-destination bookings that means N times the API calls, and providers that error on an already-deleted event (not just Google's 410) will log errors. Run the recurring cleanup once outside the loop.

findings.title: Team members' destination calendars are dropped when the organizer/event type has none
findings.body: `evt.destinationCalendar` is `null` when neither the event type nor the organizer has a destination calendar (lines 1063-1067), and line 1078 uses `evt.destinationCalendar?.push(...)`, so collective teammates' calendars collected in `teamDestinationCalendars` are silently discarded and EventManager takes the 'no destination calendar' fallback. Build the array as `[...]` first, then append the team calendars, and set it to null/[] only if the result is empty. Also, `teamDestinationCalendars` is filled inside the async `map` callbacks (lines 990-994); it only works because the push happens before the first `await`, which is fragile. Collect it with a plain loop.

findings.title: loadUsers rewrite is unrelated and changes error handling and the selected fields
findings.body: This refactor is not needed for the destinationCalendar change. An empty/missing `dynamicUserList` without an eventTypeId now throws and is turned into a 500 'Unable to load users' (previously an empty result that led to the later not-found handling). Prisma errors are re-thrown as 400 with `error.message`, which exposes DB error text to API callers. The dynamic-user select drops `organization: { select: { slug } }`, while `IsFixedAwareUser` (line 352-356) still declares `organization: { slug: string }`. The 'Don't leak to client' comment on `credentials` was also removed. Consider reverting this hunk, or splitting it into its own PR.

findings.title: Only the first destination calendar is linked to the Booking
findings.body: With collective events `evt.destinationCalendar` can hold several entries but `Booking.destinationCalendar` connects only `[0]`. Consumers that rebuild the event from the booking (confirm, cron reminder, payment webhooks, cancel, requestReschedule, all changed in this PR to wrap a single calendar in an array) therefore only ever see the organizer's calendar. Confirming a pending collective booking will thus create the calendar event only for the organizer, unlike direct booking. Confirm this is intended.

findings.title: No tests for the multi-destination-calendar behaviour
findings.body: The change alters how events are created, updated and deleted across calendar providers (credential lookup from DB, per-credential Google calendar selection, per-reference cancel). None of the changed files add or update unit/integration tests. The only test change is the e2e payload expectation. The regressions above would be caught by tests covering Meet without a destination calendar, video reference credentialId and no-externalId update/delete.

contracts.action: EventManager.create now fans out createEvent over every entry of event.destinationCalendar, loading missing credentials from the DB, and records externalId/credentialId on references
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous single-destination createAllCalendarEvents, which stored evt.destinationCalendar.externalId/credentialId on references
contracts.before_after: Before: one calendar event, references took externalCalendarId/credentialId from the destinationCalendar; video references took result.credentialId. After: one event per destination; references take result.externalId/result.credentialId; video credentialId is dropped, and the no-credentialId branch never passes externalId.
contracts.visible_effect: Calendar events for team hosts; cancellation no longer removes video meetings; events for credential-less destination calendars land in Google 'primary'
contracts.failure_mode: createEvent rejections are caught in CalendarManager and returned as success:false; DB credential lookup failures silently skip that destination

contracts.action: Cancel flow iterates all calendar references and looks up missing credentials in the DB
contracts.equivalent_path: Previous single `references.find` path in the same handler
contracts.before_after: Before: only the first calendar reference was deleted. After: every calendar reference is deleted, credential falling back to prisma.credential.findUnique; recurring-series cleanup is repeated inside the loop; Google deleteEvent fallback to destination calendar no longer matches.
contracts.visible_effect: Team hosts' calendar events are removed on cancel; duplicate delete calls for recurring bookings
contracts.failure_mode: deleteEvent promises are pushed to apiDeletes and awaited together; a rejected delete aborts the Promise.all of the rest

contracts.action: Meet-location fallback to Cal Video reads the first destination calendar's integration
contracts.before_after: Before: null-safe check; falls back to Cal Video. After: destructures from [] and dereferences undefined without optional chaining.
contracts.visible_effect: Booking creation throws for Meet bookings with no destination calendar
contracts.failure_mode: Uncaught TypeError from EventManager.create after the booking row is created

summary: The PR turns `CalendarEvent.destinationCalendar` into an array and fans calendar create, update and cancel out over it. I found three blockers. Org creation has an inverted slug condition (`create.handler.ts`). `EventManager.create` throws on a Meet location with no destination calendar. Video references lose their `credentialId`, so cancelling no longer deletes video meetings. There are also Google Calendar regressions: the hangout patch uses an undefined `calendarId`, the update/delete fallbacks never match, and destinations without a `credentialId` go to the primary calendar. The edit-location references lose `credentialId` and `externalCalendarId`. The update-failure log was removed. Team destination calendars are dropped when the organizer has none. Recurring-cancel deletion repeats per reference. No tests were added. The Lark, Office365, CalDAV/ICS, email, builder and payment/cron/tRPC call-site changes look consistent.
